title: Argand Diagrams
page_title: Argand Diagrams - A Level Maths Revision Notes

equations.alt: left parenthesis x comma space y right parenthesis

blocks.md:
- An Argand diagram is a **geometrical** way to represent complex numbers as either a **point** or a **vector** in two-dimensional space

  - We can represent the complex number $x+yi$ by the **point** with **cartesian coordinate **$(x,y)$
- The **real** component is represented by points on the **x-axis**, called the **real axis**, Re
- The **imaginary** component is represented by points on the **y-axis**, called the **imaginary axis**, Im

- You may be asked to show **roots** of an equation in an Argand diagram

  - First **solve** the equation
  - Draw a quick sketch, only adding essential information to the axes
  - Plot the points and label clearly

blocks.text: How do I sketch |z<sub>1 </sub>+ z<sub>2</sub>| and |z<sub>1 </sub>- z<sub>2</sub>|?

blocks.md:
- Plot two complex numbers *z*<sub>1 </sub>and *z*<sub>2</sub>
- Draw a line from the origin to each complex number
- Form a parallelogram using the two lines as two adjacent sides
- The modulus of their sum **|*****z***<sub>**1 **</sub>**+ *****z***<sub>**2**</sub>**| **will be the length of the diagonal of the parallelogram starting at the origin
- The modulus of their difference **|*****z***<sub>**1 **</sub>**- *****z***<sub>**2**</sub>**| **will be the length of the diagonal between the two complex numbers

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md: - When setting up an Argand diagram you do not need to draw a fully scaled axes, you only need the essential information for the points you want to show, this will save a lot of time.
